content.text: No exclusivity obligation on the Customer appears anywhere in the agreement, and § 14.16 affirmatively preserves both parties' freedom of action.

input.quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
input.rationale: Searches for exclusivity language ("exclusive", "sole", "requirements from", "procure ... from any third party", minimum-purchase commitments) surface no sole-supply or exclusive-dealing obligation on Bluefly. The only "exclusive" uses are the warranty-disclaimer heading (§ 5.2) and nonexclusive license grants in our favour (§§ 5.4, 12.1), and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) expressly confirms each party may enter into similar agreements with others, so we remain free to source hosting and related services elsewhere. Section 11.5 (Capacity Planning) and § 13.1 (Services) impose no single-source requirement, and § 14.11 restricts resale only, not our right to buy from other suppliers. This meets the preferred position; no redline needed.
